verdict: PASS for bounded synchronous token-lifetime repair
findings: Frozen oracle executed against the original before candidate or author tests were inspected. The same receiver then passed all 13 candidate contracts; the original retained 3 passing controls and 10 failures.
Actual public GET requests reuse an unexpired token at 1011.999, then refresh at 1012 after a token requested at 1000 with a 12-second lifetime and 3-second response latency.
Already-expired and malformed responses are refused before an invoice request; a separately requested next call can recover with a new valid response.
Refresh HTTP 503 propagates the identical exception before an invoice call, clears stale access, and does not replay the failed requested operation.
A separate invoice POST failure control remains one attempted operation with its existing 503 error; the constructor network gate and request shapes/timeouts stay intact.
limits: Cloud Linux CPython 3.12.14 with authored in-memory urllib responses, synthetic credentials, and a deterministic monotonic clock. No socket, real PayPal account, installed/native client, persisted invoice or payment was used. The author suite was not rerun.
